lessonRef.subject: financial-literacy
lessonRef.unitTitle: Saving, Goals, and Keeping Money Safe
lessonRef.title: Application or project: interest as a simple idea

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Financial Literacy elementary sequence — Grade 4
Manuel Academy Financial Literacy G4 Unit 4 — saving, goals, and money privacy
objective: Learners apply a simple stated interest rate to invented savings for one and two periods, and compare the result with keeping the money outside an account.
scenario: Kofi is an invented fourth grader studying a pretend savings account that pays 5% simple interest a year on the starting amount. He begins with an invented $80.00. Nothing here is a real account or a real rate.
safetyNotes: Every amount, person, business, and account in this task is invented for practice. Nothing here refers to a real household.
Never write a real bank account, card, PIN, password, Social Security, or tax number on this sheet; the task never asks for one.
This is education, not individualized financial advice. Real money decisions belong to a trusted adult.

tasks.directions: Apply the invented 5% rate to Kofi's starting $80.00 for one simulated year.

prompts.text: How much interest does one simulated year pay?

tasks.directions: Add that interest to Kofi's starting amount, then work out a second year on the same simple basis, where interest is always figured on the original $80.00.

prompts.text: What is in the simulated account after one year?
What is in the simulated account after two years?

tasks.directions: Kofi's cousin keeps the same invented $80.00 in a drawer for the two years instead.

prompts.text: How much is in the drawer after two years?
How much more does the simulated account hold after two years?

tasks.directions: The money in the drawer did no work.

prompts.text: What is Kofi actually being paid for when a simulated account adds interest to his savings?

remediation: If a learner applies the rate to the growing balance, restate the rule for Kofi in writing, that simple interest is always figured on the original amount, and mark the original amount before each year is computed.
extension: Ask the learner how many simulated years of this rate it would take for Kofi's interest alone to reach $20.00, and to justify it.
